final_message:
I implemented `tokenize`, `lookup`, `isTruthy` and `render` as the README describes. All 10 tests in `npm test` pass.

- **`src/lexer.ts`**: splits the template into text, value, `#if`, `else` and `/if` tokens. It raises `unterminated tag` when a tag is not closed.
- **`src/lookup.ts`**: `lookup` walks dotted paths through own properties of objects and arrays only. `isTruthy` uses JavaScript rules, with an empty array counted as false.
- **`src/render.ts`**: parses the tokens into a tree of text, value and if/else nodes, then renders it. Filters run left to right and are validated when the template is parsed. Values are escaped unless they use triple braces.

I also ran a few edge cases beyond the tests: `{{ constructor }}` and `{{ name.length }}` render as empty, a lone `}}` and single braces are copied through, and a second `else` throws `unexpected {{else}}`.

`tsc` is not installed and `npx tsc` failed with a registry 403, so the code has not been type-checked.

Things the README doesn't specify, which I decided on my own:
- Unknown filters are rejected when the template is parsed, so they throw even inside a branch that would not render.
- Other `{{#...}}` tags, such as `{{#each}}`, are treated as plain value expressions and render as empty rather than raising an error.
- `{{ items.length }}` returns the array length, because `length` is an own property of arrays.
